Terra correctly found that the frozen catalog is incomplete. The official food page contains omitted current products, while the separate official drink page contains many food, cocktail, beer, and wine presentations absent from Luna's catalog.
The official navigation currently links a 36-page Whiskey Bible PDF that Luna omitted as a menu surface. The PDF is restaurant-linked vendor evidence and was not fully enumerated.
No complete restaurant-issued allergen matrix or full ingredient disclosure was found. Empty arrays cannot establish negatives, and menu descriptions cannot establish complete allergen arrays.

The blanket peanut mayContain assignment is unsupported. The restaurant says peanut oil is used in its fryers, but it does not provide an item-to-fryer or shared-equipment mapping; therefore the statement cannot support peanut cross-contact conclusions for 36 individual items.

Narrow restaurant-issued positives remain valid where the menu explicitly names ingredients or unavoidable identities. Examples include peanuts, fish sauce, and crema for Brussels Sprouts; queso and creme fraiche for Barrel Nachos; eggs and cheese for the biscuits; and bread, pita, pasta, waffles, biscuits, or buns where expressly named.

The deterministic count_drift, current_only, authority_ambiguity, non_exact_reconciliation, cross_contact, validation_warnings, low_confidence, and scout_flagged_risk gates remain substantively justified, although several packet metrics materially undercount the omitted current catalog.

Terra's confirmation of the inaccessible_source gate is not supported as stated. The Whiskey Bible PDF re-opened successfully and is accessible; it is unenumerated and difficult to extract, not inaccessible.
Any interpretation that the menu descriptions prove allergen negatives or complete arrays is rejected.

Any culinary inference that adds allergens not explicit or unavoidable is rejected; examples include deriving wheat from unspecified fish sauce, wheat from an unspecified burrito tortilla, or gluten from distilled rye whiskey.

Any over-correction that removes explicit positives is rejected. In particular, Brussels Sprouts retain narrow fish, peanut, and milk evidence from the restaurant's named fish sauce, peanuts, and crema.
